Police made nearly 1,000 arrests, the government said. The Paris march began peacefully, a week after widespread rioting and looting during protests across the country. But near the demonstration's endpoint in eastern Paris, masked protesters hurled objects and fireworks at police, who answered with clouds of tear gas, deafening sound grenades and jets of water cannons. ... Ukraine and Russia eye new peace talks — and Melania Trump's mission — but steep obstacles remain KYIV, Ukraine (AP) — Ukraine and Russia have signaled their willingness to resume U.S.-brokered peace talks and are backing a humanitarian mission led by U.S. first lady Melania Trump. But deep disagreements over territory and security guarantees that re-emerged this week underscore obstacles to ending the war. The new diplomatic push comes after more than 4½ years of fighting, bringing with it a surprise announcement on Friday: Kyiv and Moscow have agreed to a local ceasefire to allow aid next week into a stranded town in Ukraine's southern war-divided region of Kherson, following secret consultations between Melania Trump and civilian negotiators from Russia and Ukraine. While the initiative raised hopes of similar humanitarian missions in the future, there were few indications that any of the key positions have shifted. Russia continues to demand Ukrainian territory it does not fully control, while Kyiv insists any agreement must include ironclad guarantees against another invasion. ... While protests in France have claimed most international attention, large demonstrations also rocked many European cities Saturday from Milan to Rome to Madrid, Lisbon and Tirana. items.title: US Business Activity Cools in October; Strong Demand Fueling Price Pressures
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Oct 23 (Reuters) - US business activity slowed modestly in ⁠October, ⁠though robust demand allowed companies to raise ⁠prices for goods and services, a sign that inflation could increase further and remain persistently high ​in the coming months. S&P Global said on Friday its flash US Composite PMI Output Index, which tracks the manufacturing and services sectors, slipped to ‌57.6 this month from a five-year high ‌reading of 58.4 in September. A reading above 50 indicates expansion in the private sector. Strength in manufacturing was offset by a ⁠slight pullback in ⁠the vast services sector. The PMI suggested the economy started the fourth quarter on solid ​footing following what is expected to have been a strong performance in the July-September quarter. Economists expect the government's advance gross domestic product report next week to show the economy growing at around a 3.0% annualized rate last quarter, mainly driven by consumer spending and business investment in AI. The ​economy has so far not shown any signs of buckling under the weight of the oil price shock stemming from ⁠the ⁠US-Israeli war with Iran, with savings, ⁠generous tax returns in ​the spring, tariff refunds, a strong stock market performance and corporate profits providing a cushion. Economists warned that the inflation ​fallout from the drawn-out Middle East ⁠conflict was likely to slow consumer spending this quarter. The survey's measure of new orders received by businesses edged up to 58.2 this month, the highest level since March 2022, from 58.1 in September. The increase was mostly in the services sector, with S&P Global noting "rising domestic demand, boosted partly by precautionary stock building" and growth in exports. ... Its gauge of prices for output rose to 59.8, the highest reading ⁠since August 2022, from 58.4 in September. Businesses across manufacturing and services sectors raised prices. Delivery performance by ⁠suppliers to manufacturers deteriorated further. The survey's measure of suppliers' delivery times dropped to a more than four-year low of 38.1 from 40.9 in September. ... "Cost pressures remain a key concern," said Chris Williamson, chief business economist at S&P Global Market Intelligence. "Supply chain bottlenecks have meanwhile intensified, and order book backlogs are growing, making it easier for companies to pass higher costs on to customers." ... Consumer and producer prices increased strongly in September, the government reported this month, raising concerns that inflation was fanning out across the economy. The Federal Reserve in September raised its overnight benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to the 3.75%-4.00% range.

items.excerpt: President Trump has endorsed Benjamin Netanyahu in Tuesday's Israeli election, but some of his advisers see opportunity for his Middle East agenda in a government led by someone else, U.S. officials tell Axios.

By Eli Yokley | Twitter Email (eyokley@morningconsult.com) Was this email forwarded to you? You can subscribe here for free to get this sent to your inbox twice a week. President Donald Trump’s net approval rating improved 3 percentage points over the past week, with 46% approving and 51% disapproving in our latest tracker update. That improvement comes as the federal government’s Oct. 1 shutdown remains our most salient story for the third week in a row. It’s just the latest indication that, as we get into more below, the impasse on Capitol Hill may be full of sound and fury, but signifies nothing for the average voter. 36% ... Less than a quarter of voters have seen, read or heard “a lot” about Trump’s construction of a new $250 million ballroom at the White House, but that might soon increase. As The Washington Post reported yesterday under a striking image shared by a source, demolition crews began ripping down part of the presidential mansion’s East Wing despite Trump’s pledge that the pending 90,000-square-foot structure wouldn’t interfere or touch the existing building. Shutdown Trump is set to host Senate Republicans for lunch at the White House today “to celebrate their unity in the government shutdown fight and for passing nominees,” according to Politico, which noted that the party’s push for a Nov. 21 funding extension may need to change as Washington gets closer to the expiration date. Some conservatives are said to be pushing for a continuing resolution that would run until March or even next October, though the idea irks Senate Appropriations Committee Chair Susan Collins (R-Maine). Perhaps most notably: NOTUS reports that some Republican senators — even Collins herself — are beginning to entertain the idea of employing the nuclear option to pass a continuing resolution with a simple majority. On the Obamacare front, Politico also reports that Republicans are ramping up talks with the White House on what kind of premium tax credit expansion the party could support once the government is reopened. The party is said to be considering a year-end health care policy package with a two-year extension of scaled-back ACA subsidies though it’s uncertain how that would be received in the House. Nominees The New York Times reports that Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-S.D.) is among at least four Republican senators who have come out in opposition to Trump’s nomination of Paul Ingrassia to lead the Office of Special Counsel following a Politico report documenting a series of racist text messages. That’s enough Republicans to kill Ingrassia’s nomination even before his planned testimony to the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee on Thursday. Separately, Axios noted that Trump has paused the nomination of former Florida Deputy Attorney General John Guard to fill an open open judicial seat in the Middle District of Florida over his connection with a criminal probe, and The Wall Street Journal points out a “power struggle” between Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Elon Musk-aligned billionaire Jared Isaacman over the stewardship of NASA. Gerrymandering House Democratic leaders in Washington have devised a new congressional boundary map for Illinois that would target Republican Rep. Darin LaHood, aiming to reduce the state’s GOP-leaning districts to two, Punchbowl News reports on the party’s response to GOP gerrymandering efforts. Legislators will be in a veto session next week, but will have to move fast ahead of Illinois' pending filing deadline or move next year’s primary date. U.S.-China Trump has rolled out a list of topics he expects to discuss when he meets next week with Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in South Korea. He pointed to rare earth minerals, fentanyl, soybeans and Taiwan, “underlining the divisive topics the two sides plan to tackle at the negotiating table as a fragile trade truce nears its expiration,” as Bloomberg News put it. ... The stalemate between Republicans and Democrats on Capitol Hill over how to reopen the federal government is mirrored by how voters are analyzing what’s happening in Washington. The situation is largely unchanged since we checked in on which side voters blame, and neither have the numbers. ... Our fresh tracking data shows that voters are 10 points more likely to say responsibility for the shutdown lies with Republicans in Congress rather than Democrats (46% to 36%), in line with the 11-point spread we measured last week. Shares of voters who blame the following for the shutdown: ... Republican voters, who began the shutdown blaming Democrats by a 15-point margin, are only 9 points more likely to do so today. They’re also 10 points more likely to blame their own side of the aisle than Democrats are (40% to 30%), compared with a 3-point gap we measured in the first survey. While voters are more likely to blame Republicans on Capitol Hill for the shutdown, very little has changed about their popularity, or the popularity of Democrats in Congress. ... On the political front, our read on the generic congressional ballot went unmoved over the past week, with 46% of voters indicating their support for the hypothetical Democratic candidate and 43% backing the unnamed Republican candidate if the midterm elections were held today. By these metrics, the party out of power is winning the shutdown fight — or at least holding its own — when it comes to public sentiment. But Washington’s standoff, to date, has left many Americans thinking a lot like they did before the shutdown began.

items.title: Charli xcx Joins Martin Scorsese's 'What Happens at Night'
items.excerpt: Charli xcx and Martin Scorsese‘s collaboration is extending beyond the cover for her new album “Music, Fashion, Film.” Sources tell Variety that the pop star has a cameo in the Oscar-winning director’s upcoming movie “What Happens at Night” alongside Leonardo DiCaprio and Jennifer Lawrence. Described as a Gothic psychological drama, the Apple and StudioCanal production follows an American married couple who travel to a small European town to adopt a baby — but as they struggle to claim their child, the less they seem to know about themselves. Charli’s part in the film is being kept under wraps. She joins a cast that also includes Mads Mikkelsen, Patricia Clarkson and Jared Harris.

items.title: HYBE Cine Fest 2026 Cinema Event Going Global With 2 Live BTS Broadcasts
items.excerpt: The HYBE Cine Fest is going international this year with a weeklong global event hitting theaters in more than 60 territories from Oct. 24-31. After launching in Latin America in 2024 and expanding to Asia in 2025, this year’s collaboration between Trafalgar Releasing and HYBE will feature six different events, including the first-ever airings of two BTS live broadcasts from South America. The BTS WORLD TOUR ‘ARIRANG’ in Buenos Aires: Live Viewing in cinemas will mark the K-pop supergroup’s first-ever performance in Argentina, with screenings slated for Oct. 24 in the Americas and Oct. 25 in the rest of the world. A second BTS show, ARIRANG in SÃO PAULO: Live Viewing, will mark the grand finale of the boy band’s Latin American tour, with screenings slated for Oct. 30 in the Americas and Oct. 31 in the rest of the world. “Following the incredible response to HYBE CINE FEST across Latin America and Asia, we are scaling this festival format to global cinema audiences,” said Trafalgar Releasing CEO Marc Allenby in a statement. “Bringing together major concert films, interactive 3D cheering parties and landmark live broadcasts across a single week gives fans everywhere an unprecedented way to celebrate their favorite HYBE artists together in cinemas.” ... The program will also feature screenings of SEVENTEEN’s WORLD TOUR ‘NEW_’ concert film marking the group’s 10th anniversary, as well as TOMORROW X TOGETHER’s ACT : TOMORROW from that band’s fourth world tour. The programming will including a screening of the Seoul kick-off of ENHYPEN’S BLOOD SAGA WORLD TOUR and a HYBE Cheering Party (in 3D) where fans are encouraged to chant and sing along to 3D-enhanced on-screen lyrics and wave their official light sticks to music videos of their favorite HYBE acts (LE SSERAFIM, &TEAM, BOYNEXTDOOR, TWS, ILLIT, KATSEYE, aoen, CORTIS and SANTOS BRAVOS). Tickets go on sale worldwide on Sept. 30 at 9 a.m. ET, with specific programming schedules, regional showtimes and ticketing information available here. The BTS live viewing broadcasts will be anchored to specific live and delayed broadcast times (available here), while all the other festival titles will screen from Oct. 24-31.

The tour yielded a Disney+ Concert Special and the Descendants/ZOMBIES: Worlds Collide Tour – The Live Album. ... The 2026 tour builds on that momentum. The all-new “ Worlds Collide Concert Tour” brings together the worlds of “ Descendants,” “ZOMBIES,” and for the very first time, “ Camp Rock,” in an unforgettable new arena spectacular. A pop concert of the highest caliber, this year’s cast features an exceptionally talented lineup of Disney stars including Malachi Barton (“ZOMBIES 4,” “Camp Rock 3”), Liamani Segura (“Descendants: Wicked Wonderland,” “Camp Rock 3”), Dara Reneé (“Descendants: The Rise of Red”), Mekonnen Knife (“ZOMBIES 4”), Hudson Stone (“Camp Rock 3”), Swayam Bhatia (“ZOMBIES 4”), Kiara Romero (“Descendants: Wicked Wonderland”), and Alexandro Byrd (“Descendants: Wicked Wonderland”). Fans will experience an evening packed with hit songs from all three franchises brought together in a brand-new production with fresh mashups and fan favorite songs. Next-level choreography and electrifying special effects create an evening filled with nonstop delight, fan interactions, and nostalgia. Come dressed as your favorite character, sing along all night, and experience the music and moments from “ Descendants,” “ZOMBIES” and “Camp Rock” colliding on stage in this all-new concert experience.
